blocks.text: 研究人员在通过庞大 AI 服务网络发送的请求中埋下了 200 万个数字追踪标记，想弄清托付给这些服务的敏感信息究竟去了哪里。结果他们发现，这个生态系统泄露高度敏感数据简直像筛子一样。

inlines.text: 研究人员在通过庞大 AI 服务网络发送的请求中埋下了 200 万个数字追踪标记，想弄清托付给这些服务的敏感信息究竟去了哪里。结果他们发现，这个生态系统泄露高度敏感数据简直像筛子一样。

blocks.text: 这一暴露是通过一项巧妙的实验发现的，该实验旨在检验敏感信息是否会经由大量广泛使用的 AI 服务链条泄露，以及一旦泄露，这些信息又是如何被利用的。如今许多 AI 应用会使用 OpenRouter 或 Vercel 这类充当中间商的服务。这些“AI 路由器”（有时也叫“AI 网关”）接收 AI 应用终端用户发来的大量提示词，再根据最低收费、最适合当前任务等标准，把它们路由到可用的推理引擎。开发者不用 Anthropic、OpenAI 或其他大厂，而是雇一个 AI 路由器来寻找最合适的模型。

blocks.text: 11 月 21 日更新：Hacker News 和 X 上的帖子都称，OpenRouter 已向客户发送邮件，通知他们部分提示词可能已被读取。OpenRouter 援引了这项研究，称收到一份报告，指出潜在暴露涉及发送给中国模型提供商 MiniMax 的提示词。OpenRouter 表示，无论提示词是直接发给 MiniMax，还是经由 AtlasCloud、Novita 和 StreamLake 这三家转售商发送，研究人员埋下的 URL 都被访问过。OpenRouter 已移除 MiniMax 模型端点上的“零数据保留”标签。鸣谢：Sulat.com。

blocks.text: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

inlines.text: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

blocks.text: The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

blocks.text: Update, Nov 21: Posts on both Hacker News and X report that OpenRouter has sent customers an email notifying them that some of their prompts may have been read. OpenRouter cited the research and said that it received a report that the potential exposure involved prompts sent to MiniMax, a China-based model provider. OpenRouter said the researchers' planted URLs were accessed whether the prompts were sent to MiniMax directly or through three other resellers: AtlasCloud, Novita, and StreamLake. OpenRouter has removed a "Zero Data Retention" label from MiniMax-model endpoints. Hat tip: Sulat.com.
